How to read this report

Only VerihoggFormat warnings from sv-tests logs are analyzed. Causes are grouped into tokens, constructs, annotation issues, and other codes.

Occurrences

Total number of times the cause appears in the logs.

Tests

Number of distinct tests that contain the cause at least once.

Solo

Warning tests where this cause is the only parsed cause. A test with end and real counts toward Tests for both, but toward Solo for neither.

Greedy #

An ordering, not a count. At each step, pick the cause that would close the most still-open warning tests if it were the only remaining blocker; remove those tests and repeat. Ties are broken by occurrence count. Cumulative shows how many tests would be clean after fixing causes 1..N.

Example. A has only end; B has end and real; C has real and or.
  • Solo: end=1, real=0, or=0.
  • Greedy: end (+1, A), real (+1, B), or (+1, C); cumulative 1, 2, 3.

Why this is a heuristic. A test can contain several unsupported constructs; fixing one may leave other warnings or expose a new warning on the same or another line. The logs describe current formatter output, not the result of a future patch. Causes such as bracket and macro are often secondary symptoms. Treat Newly clean as simulated coverage, not as a guarantee that the test will pass.

By test suite

Suite is the sv-tests results_group: main = tests from the SV Tests repository, cores = generated tests for third-party cores, imported = imported third-party test suites. Tests without a group are shown as main.
